response.shapeSummary: Live award-mode probing confirmed an available paginated JSON response with spending_level, limit, results, page_metadata, and messages. Each award row contains the requested field-label columns plus helper identifiers such as internal_id, generated_internal_id, awarding_agency_id, and agency_slug; a 2026-05-14 richer contract outlier screen also returned Awarding Sub Agency, Funding Agency, Funding Sub Agency, Contract Award Type, Start Date, End Date, and Last Modified Date in the same row set. For prime-award handoff, raw API rows materially surface generated_internal_id only. This bundle models canonical_award_lookup_id as a derived semantic alias for that same returned string rather than as a second live payload key, so callers should not expect both names in raw JSON.

observed.notes: Reviewer-backed live screening showed only generated_internal_id in raw search output; canonical_award_lookup_id is the bundle alias for that same returned string. The selected 2026-05-16 AI-keyword competition story reconfirmed that live rows for W911QX20C0023 and W911QX25C0002 surfaced generated_internal_id but no visible canonical_award_lookup_id field, and those same strings still worked unchanged as award-detail handoff ids. The richer 2026-05-14 contract outlier screen also returned the underlying generated_internal_id, so callers can keep the same canonical handoff while adding more visible screening columns.

quirks.statement: Result rows use API-defined field labels instead of a stable snake_case schema, and the exact label set depends on spending_level plus award type family.
quirks.impact: Callers must treat the fields array as part of the response contract, not just as a projection hint.

quirks.statement: Some requested labels map to structured response objects rather than scalars, including NAICS, PSC, Recipient Location, Primary Place of Performance, Sub-Recipient Location, and Sub-Award Primary Place of Performance.
quirks.impact: Do not assume every requested field value is a plain string or number.

quirks.statement: The same downstream award-handoff business key is labeled differently across related workflows: spending_by_award emits generated_internal_id, award detail guidance discusses generated_unique_award_id or generated_internal_id, and award funding accepts the same value under request field award_id.
quirks.impact: Normalize that cross-endpoint handoff value as canonical_award_lookup_id within this bundle, but if you inspect raw search JSON the literal field to read is generated_internal_id; pass that same string unchanged into downstream award detail or award funding requests.

quirks.statement: Reviewer-backed live evidence covers a bounded keyword-led contract preview path when filters.keywords is paired with explicit award_type_codes.
quirks.impact: For paired preview-to-download workflows, add award_type_codes on search instead of assuming download defaults carry over unchanged.

gaps.statement: The endpoint docs defer important nested object details such as location objects and time-period variants to shared search_filters documentation instead of fully defining them inline.
gaps.impact: Highly specific nested filters may need extra validation or shared-doc lookup before use.

risks.statement: Large result sets are expensive and the source enforces sequential search_after pagination for deep result windows.
risks.impact: Use bounded limit values and prefer downloads for bulk extraction workflows.

risks.statement: Requested field labels, sort compatibility, and valid award_type_codes interact with each other and can produce validation errors when mixed incorrectly.
risks.impact: Reuse known-good field sets and keep award families consistent within a request.

risks.statement: Live responses can include a warning that search time periods are currently limited to an earliest date of 2007-10-01.
risks.impact: Older historical analysis may need download endpoints instead of award search.

risks.statement: Display Award ID values are human-facing labels and are not the most reliable cross-endpoint handoff key when generated_internal_id is present on a prime-award row.
risks.impact: Using the display label instead of raw generated_internal_id or the bundle alias canonical_award_lookup_id can make award-detail or funding drilldowns fragile.

handoffKeys.name: canonical_award_lookup_id
handoffKeys.description: For prime-award search rows, treat the raw generated_internal_id value as the canonical downstream award lookup id. This bundle normalizes that same returned string as canonical_award_lookup_id for award detail and funding handoffs.

targetEndpoints.description: Pass the same string unchanged as the award detail path award_id.
Pass the same string unchanged as the funding request award_id.

measureInterpretations.name: Award Amount
measureInterpretations.meaning: In bounded time_period searches, Award Amount remains the award-level size on each matched row rather than a current-period spend subtotal. The row can appear because of in-period activity or updates even when visible award dates are much older than the filtered window.
measureInterpretations.safeUse: Use Award Amount to rank or screen large awards, then pair it with Start Date, End Date, and Last Modified Date while treating the row as an activity-screen match until follow-up confirms period meaning.
measureInterpretations.unsafeUse: Do not publish Award Amount from this search row as fiscal-year spend or as the amount of the in-period transaction, modification, or funding event that caused inclusion.
measureInterpretations.dashboardWarning: Bounded time_period screens can surface clearly legacy awards such as DEAC3243AL00036; keep Award Amount labeled as lifetime award size on the matched row until award detail or funding follow-up supports a current-period interpretation.

recommendedFollowups.trigger: A bounded time_period search hit looks legacy, already ended, or otherwise risky to describe as a new current-period award.
recommendedFollowups.reason: Confirm date_signed and period_of_performance before describing the matched row as a newly signed award or using it in a current-period narrative.

recommendedFollowups.trigger: You need current-period spending meaning or funding evidence instead of reusing Award Amount from the search row.
recommendedFollowups.reason: Use award_id with the same canonical award lookup value to inspect downstream funding slices rather than interpreting Award Amount as a bounded-period spend subtotal.
